text:
B: Hello, hi. Can you hear me?
A: Yeah, hello. I'm Darren.
B: Claire. Nice to meet you. Where are you calling from?
A: Kesgrave, near Ipswich. You?
B: Catford, South East London. What do you do, Darren?
A: Gas engineer. Boilers, heating. Self-employed, one van, about fourteen years.
B: Oh, I'll be honest, I guessed something like that. You reminded me of some of the contractors I work with.
A: Ha, is that good or bad?
B: Mostly good. Depends on the contractor. I'm a housing officer, so I'm the one ringing them to ask why a boiler's still not fixed after three weeks.
A: Ah. So you're the enemy, then.
B: Sort of, yeah. I've got a family at the moment with a toddler and no heating, and the contractor keeps sending someone out to top up the pressure and leave. It drives me mad.
A: Yeah, that's the cheap fix, that. Usually it's a leak or the expansion vessel. Topping it up just buys you a fortnight.
B: That's what I thought. Why do they keep doing it, then?
A: Erm, honestly? Those contracts are priced tight. The firm gets a fixed rate per call-out, so the bloke's got eight jobs that day and he does the quickest thing. Not saying it's right, but that's how it works.
B: That's really useful, actually. I can push them on the vessel. Do you do much housing association work?
A: Not really. Mostly private, homeowners. Better money, to be fair, and they don't argue the bill as much.
B: I bet. How do you price things? I always wonder whether quotes are, you know, fair.
A: Ha, depends who's asking. No, it's parts, labour, bit for the van. Everyone does it a bit different. I keep my customers happy, that's the main thing.
B: Fair enough. Is it busy at this time of year?
A: Winter's mad. January I was doing twelve-hour days. Knees are feeling it now.
B: I've got a dodgy knee from running, so I swim instead. Ladywell, early mornings, and the lido when it's warm enough.
A: Lido, in this country? Rather you than me.
B: It's freezing until about June, but it's lovely once you're in. Do you do anything to switch off?
A: Walk the dog, Bailey. Round the heath. Bit of golf, and Ipswich on telly. And a barbecue in the summer, I've got a new gas one I'm quite pleased with.
B: A gas engineer with a gas barbecue, that's very on brand.
A: Ha, never thought of it like that. You go away much?
B: Erm, trains, mostly. Ghent, Bruges, Lisbon last autumn. I try not to fly if I can help it.
A: Lisbon on a train? How long's that take?
B: Two days, sort of. With stops. I had a spreadsheet.
A: Blimey. I'll stick to the plane to Turkey, I think. Pool, all-inclusive, job done.
B: That's fair. I think we're nearly out of time.
A: Yeah, think so. Good luck with that boiler, Claire. Ask about the vessel.
B: I will. Thanks, Darren, that was genuinely helpful.
